g: (wiki jargon, chiefly Wikimedia jargon, metonymic) An unregistered user identified by their IP address.
This IP made a disruptive edit!
(US, military, initialism, slang) An Iraqi police officer, or the Iraqi police as a whole.

(Internet) A number assigned to each computer's or other device's network interface, which are active on a network. supporting the Internet Protocol, in order to distinguish each network interface, and hence each networked device) from every other network interface anywhere on the network.
A wireless webcam used specifically for surveillance as a security measure.
(Internet) A protocol for sending IP packets over an existing IP network.
IP in IP is an unusual mechanism: not only does it use two network layers, it uses the same protocol on both.
(mathematics) A set of natural numbers that contains all finite sums of some infinite set.
(computing, networking) Software that converts an IP address into a hostname and provides location and other information.
(linguistics, countable) A transcription written in the International Phonetic Alphabet.
(computing, countable) A kind of archive containing a software package for certain Apple devices. Originally an initialism of iPhone Archive, later redefined as iOS App Store Package.
(trademark) A lightweight low-power tablet computer of a particular range from Apple Inc.
He was watching a movie on his iPad.
(by extension) Any lightweight low-power tablet computer.
(Internet slang, sometimes mildly derogatory) A child, generally Generation Alpha, who gets all of their entertainment through an iPad or other tablet; a child who is addicted to using their tablet.
That iPad kid went ballistic in the restaurant after his mom took his iPad away.
(slang, derogatory, neologism) A parent who allows their child near-unlimited (usually unsupervised) screen time; a parent who lets a tablet computer, such as an iPad, raise their child.
A kinase inhibitor proposed as a preventer of breast cancer
A type of wood of the genus Tabebuia, similar to teak, used for outdoor decking and furniture.
The dried rhizome and roots of either of two tropical American plants (Cephaelis acuminata and Cephaelis ipecacuanha) of the madder family used especially as a source of emetine.
(pharmacology) An emetic and expectorant drug that contains emetine and is prepared from ipecac especially as a syrup for use in treating accidental poisoning.
The shrub that produces ipecac (Cephaelis ipecacuanha), native to Brazil and cultivated elsewhere.
(medicine, pharmacology) The root of Carapichea ipecacuanha, used as an emetic or purgative; a preparation of this root used as a drug; ipecac.
(medicine, pharmacology) The flowering plant Carapichea ipecacuanha.
(organic chemistry) A pseudotannin found in ipecacuanha.
A neuroprotective drug that is a glutamate antagonist.
(trademark) A smartphone of a series produced by Apple, which typically combine a camera phone, PDA, multimedia player, and wireless communication device.
His mom bought him an IPhone for his 11th birthday.
(by extension) Any knockoff or similar high-end smartphone; through trademark genericization.
(Internet slang, neologism) A face that is inappropriate for a period drama.
The moment when a company or industry realizes that it needs to catch up with apparent technological and scientific developments made by some other company or industry.
The use of an iPhone to take photographs.
A Philippine and Pacific island tree (Intsia bijuga) yielding a valuable brown dye and having a very hard and durable dark wood.
(pharmacology) A human monoclonal antibody being developed as a drug to activate the immune system.
(ichthyology) Any fish in the family Ipnopidae of deepsea tripod fishes.
(intransitive, transitive) To launch an initial public offering, to go public.
(trademark) A portable music player made by Apple.
(by extension) Any portable personal MP3 player or similar device.
(slang, taxation) A levy or tax on digital storage products (e.g. iPods), levied at a per unit capacity rate, used to compensate content providers for piracy of their goods.
(slang, rare) The process of making technology simpler or easier to use by reducing the complexity of a device or its user interface
A naturally occurring iridoid glycoside found in a number of plants including Stachytarpheta dichotoma and Plantago euphratica.
(organic chemistry) A diketone derivative of furan, produced by Ceratostomella fimbriata, a mold that grows on sweet potato, 1-(furan-3-yl)pentane-1,4-dione
(botany) Any of various twining plants of the genus Ipomoea with showy monopetalous flowers, including the morning glory, the sweet potato, and the cypress vine.
(organic chemistry) A glucoside obtained from Ipomoea pandurata.
Any virus, of the genus Ipomovirus, that infect sweet potatoes (of the genus Ipomoea)
The tuber of any one of several edible species of Perideridia spp.
A mythical creature depicted as a half-human, half-horse that is supposedly different from a centaur, sometimes attributed to Greek mythology.
(Japanese mahjong) A yaku awarded for winning before the end of the player's next turn after declaring riichi
(martial arts, judo) The highest score in judo, awarded for a throw that places the opponent on their back with impetus or for holding the opponent on their back for a number of seconds.

An anticholinergic drug C₂₀H₃₀NO₃⁺ that is used as an inhalational aerosol for bronchodilation especially in the treatment of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and as a nasal spray in the treatment of runny nose associated with rhinitis.
A serotonin antagonist used as an antimigraine agent.
A hydrazine drug previously used as an antidepressant, known to cause fulminant hepatitis.
A hydrazine drug formerly used as an antidepressant.
(pharmacology) An antiprotozoal nitroimidazole drug used in veterinary medicine.
An azapirone with anxiolytic and antidepressant properties.
(psychology) Denoting a measure that forces a person to choose among multiple desirable options.
Myers-Briggs uses ipsative measures, whereas the Five-Factor Model uses normative measures.
(education) Comparing a measure of a person against that person’s previous assessments, rather than against the performance of others.
A terpene alcohol found in bark beetles of the genus Ips.
(rhetoric) A dogmatic and unproved proposition or dictum that is accepted solely on the authority of someone who is known to have asserted it.
An authority who makes such an assertion.
(countable) An unfounded, false and dogmatic assertion; an ipse dixit.
(uncountable) The practice of making such assertions.
One who makes unfounded, false and dogmatic assertions.
(psychiatry) A symptom of schizophrenia spectrum disorders characterized by disturbances in the patient's sense of self.
(medicine) Occurring in, or involving the same hemisphere, usually of the cerebrum.
(anatomy, medicine) On the same side of the body.
The stroke was characterised by ipsilateral paralysis.
(medicine) The state of being ipsilateral, i.e. being on the same side.
(anatomy, medicine) On the same side of the body.
Dorsal columns carry mechanoreceptor information ipsilaterally.
(pathology, medicine) On the same side as a lesion.
On the same side as a lesion.
(medicine) Pulsion towards the side of the lesion.
who has not been sick to death of everything subjective and its accursed ipsissimosity!
Being such by itself, or by its own definition; inherent.
By that very fact itself; actually.
Of an intersex person: identifying with the sex they were medically assigned; having a gender which matches their assigned sex.
For quotations using this term, see Citations:ipso gender.
A well-marked subspecies of the Savannah sparrow.
(organic chemistry, pharmacology) A medication used to treat paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria.
(organic chemistry) Any of a group of polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons composed of arene subunits bound to a bridged bicyclooctatriene core
A percussion instrument made from hollowed gourds, often used to provide a beat for hula dancing.
Belief in the Invisible Pink Unicorn.
